reason: The exposed fittings need shelter, and the fired bricks seem suited to building a freestanding wall at the cabin perimeter.
expectation: I expect to build a brick shelter around the water-line area, though it may need additional insulation.

alternatives.reason: Wrapping the line could also protect it, but the goal and chapter title point toward building a wall.

effect: The wall stands independently, so local material can be packed against it without loading the cabin.
reaction: The separate footing makes the wall’s purpose clearer.
reason: The result points to packing local material against the wall, and the shovel seems suited to that work.
expectation: I expect to pack material against the wall to help shelter the water line, though I’m unsure whether insulation will also be needed.

alternatives.reason: Insulating the line also seems useful, but I want to finish the wall shelter first.

effect: The berm now shields the service connections from drifting grit while keeping them accessible. The remaining combination may provide additional protection for the line.
reaction: The removable covers are a satisfying detail because the connections still need to be reached.
reason: This is the only available combination, and wrapping the water line with quilt stock seems useful for insulation.
expectation: I expect the quilt stock to insulate the connected well line, though I’m unsure how it will fit with the existing heated jacket.

effect: The quilt insulates the existing heating jacket, but the line still needs protection from drifting grit.
reaction: I am curious how the shovel will shelter the exposed couplings while keeping them accessible.
reason: The shovel is the only available gameplay option, and the result says the line needs protection from grit.
expectation: I expect to use local material to shelter the insulated line and its connections, though I am unsure exactly how.

effect: The trench shelters the insulated hose while keeping its connections accessible. The covering slows heat loss, but the heat tracing still needs power.
reaction: The distinction between insulation and powered heating was useful; I also liked that the connections remain accessible.

mostWorthwhile.text: Trenching the insulated line was most worthwhile because it brought the protection together and explained what insulation can and cannot do.

leastWorthwhile.text: Wrapping the line was fairly predictable after the wall was built, especially as it was the only available combination.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the insulated wrapping still lay on open ground after the berm had sheltered the service connections; the hose needed a separate trench.

arbitrary.text: The shovel action was suggested by the remaining option, but exactly how it would protect the line was unclear until the trench appeared.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because the practical details about protecting equipment on Mars make me curious about the next problem and how the expedition unfolds.
